analysis.title: Morning Briefing - The Day After
key_insights: Hot October US CPI plus hawkish Fed speak lifted 2y UST yields 18bp to 4.738% and 10y UST to 4.99% (from 4.855%), with resistance at 5.02%. 2s/10s flattened to 25bp. Fed December pricing is +28bp and January +44bp.
Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m for the third straight month in October, taking the annual rate to 2.6%, the highest since June. Core services ex-rent rose to 3.52%, the highest since May.

SG notes FOMC member Waller raised the case for a 50bp hike in December 'to ensure its credibility'. In the last dot-plot only four of eighteen members pencilled in 50bp to 4.375% by year end. The odds of a 50bp move in one go rose to just over 10%.

SG says a 25bp hike before the midterms may have generated less volatility than the positioning could now cause over Thanksgiving. Further repricing may depend on PCE inflation on the 25th. SG economics keep their call for hikes in December and March.

SG asks whether markets are repeating the late-90s playbook into 2027: curve inversion, tighter financial conditions, slower growth and earnings momentum, and a stronger dollar at least in the short term.
The 10y UST refunding auction was soft: tail of 0.9bp, non-dealer bidding 90.2%, bid-to-cover 2.46x, and the lowest indirect bidding since Oct-23.

Fed speakers: Logan said faster hikes may be needed, Goolsbee called the CPI report 'borderline disturbing', Bowman said more confidence is needed given AI-related risks, and Paulson called gradual tightening appropriate for now.
USD/JPY is bid after closing above its 200dma (158.69) for the first time since 14 October. The 2y UST/JGB spread widened to 298.5bp (+22bp intraday). Support 156.96, resistance 160.39.
EUR/USD keeps a bearish bias in a 1.1151-1.1170 range, with support at 1.1100 and resistance at 1.1255. Large option expiries sit at 1.1100 (€3.8bn) and 1.120-50 (€8.1bn).

GBP/USD stays offered below the 50dma (1.3353) after a bearish outside day. AUD/USD dip buyers are defending the late March low of 0.6834, and Australian 3Q new housing loan commitments fell 15.5%, the largest quarterly decline on record.
UK 10y IRS surged 10bp yesterday tracking US rates. December MPC pricing is 16bp. NIESR sees inflation not returning to 2% before late 2030, about two years later than the OBR and BoE projections.

Hungary's October headline inflation rose to 2.0% from 1.6%, driven by fuel, while core rose 0.4% m/m, below forecast. SG's base case is an MNB hold at 5.5% in November and a possible 25bp cut in December, conditional on oil falling toward $80/bbl.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Third successive 0.3% monthly gain, which pushed Fed hike pricing higher.
Declined since the last FOMC meeting, which supports the case for further tightening.
Market-implied. January pricing is +44bp, and the odds of a single 50bp move are just over 10%.
Only a minority of members favor a 50bp move.
Up from 1.6% on fuel prices. Monthly core data was softer than forecast.
SG base case is a hold, with a possible 25bp cut in December.

risk_factors: A move to 50bp in a single December hike would add year-end liquidity strain.
PCE inflation on the 25th and PPI on Friday may drive further repricing of Fed hikes.
Weak 10y UST refunding auction demand, with indirect bidding the lowest since Oct-23.
A stronger dollar, curve inversion and tighter financial conditions into 2027 would slow growth and earnings, as in the late 90s.
Oil above $80/bbl would limit the MNB's room to cut in December.
charts_described: Chart of the day plots the 2s/10s UST spread against inversion, with the 2s/10s at 25bp.
vol_and_positioning: SG says positioning could cause market tension over Thanksgiving if the Fed delivers a 50bp hike in December. Year-end liquidity conditions are typically poor.
Option expiries to define today's ranges: EUR/USD 1.1100 (€3.8bn) and 1.120-50 (€8.1bn), USD/JPY 158.95-159.00 ($625m), EUR/GBP 0.8325-50 (€1.2bn) and 0.8365-80 (€340m).

tension_points.bull_case: A 50bp hike in December would reinforce the Fed's credibility, as Waller argued, and Logan said faster hikes may be needed. Hot CPI lifted December pricing to +28bp.
tension_points.bear_case: Only four of eighteen members pencilled in 50bp in the last dot-plot, and SG says a 50bp move would cause drama in thin year-end liquidity. SG economics keep their call for 25bp hikes in December and March.
tension_points.what_invalidates: PCE inflation on the 25th, which SG says decides whether further repricing toward 50bp is warranted.
